articles.title: Manchester United Muslim fans group calls on co-owner Jim Ratcliffe to quit
articles.summary: Supporters’ club says billionaire should stand down after ‘completely unacceptable’ comments on the UK and empire. Manchester United’s Muslim supporters’ Club (MUMSC) has called for the Premier League side’s co-owner to step down after he made “completely unacceptable” comments during a BBC…
body: Sir Jim Ratcliffe described the UK as being a country “on the slide” from the days when it had “the greatest empire in the world”.

In what was described as a “statement of no confidence” posted on X, MUMSC said: “Our players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds. Manchester United would not be Manchester United without them.
“Manchester United does not belong emotionally to investment funds, shareholders or billionaires.
“After years of decline, broken promises and repeated failure, Manchester United Muslim Supporters’ Club has lost confidence in the current ownership structure of Manchester United Football Club.

articles.title: ‘They deserved to win’: Mikel Arteta left humbled by Brighton defeat
articles.summary: Arsenal’s 100% start to season comes to an end. Manager says team put themselves in trouble from start. Mikel Arteta admitted Arsenal were taught a lesson by free-scoring Brighton as their 100% start to the season was abruptly ended on Saturday.
body: “They deserved to win the game and it’s a big lesson for us,” said a disappointed Arteta, who felt his players were not their usual combative selves. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.
“We put ourselves in trouble one time, two times, three times and we need to get out of that much quicker than that. That’s one of the biggest lessons that we have to take from the game.

“We knew how tough it was going to be and the first thing we had discussed was about the first part. If you don’t get out of that first part as winners, it will be extremely difficult to dominate the game and to have any probability of winning the game. At this level, it’s extremely important to respect and to understand [that] before anything else.”

articles.title: De Zerbi rips into Spurs players after Villa defeat: ‘Disappointed, sad and frustrated’
articles.summary: Tottenham lose 3-2 at home with two late consolations. ‘We can’t lose the game in this way,’ says furious manager. Roberto De Zerbi tore into his failing Tottenham team after their 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa, saying “we can’t lose the game in this way”.
body: De Zerbi criticised his team’s mentality, but also the physical condition of his players, and said the substitute Mohammed Kudus had disrupted the balance of his team.

“I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated for the performance,” De Zerbi said. “We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal, we can’t lose balance just because we are losing. I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.”

Jackson scored in the 67th minute after latching on to a long kick by the impressive Zion Suzuki. De Zerbi said his players had been prepped to deal with the Villa goalkeeper’s clearances, but had switched off.

“We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season and we spoke in many meetings about it,” De Zerbi said. “Now we have to explain another game like [the home defeat against] Newcastle where we played the first half well, got to 60 minutes OK, and then we lose.”

articles.title: Blaze win One-Day Cup in last-ball thriller
articles.summary: Emma Jones seals the Blaze's treble success with a dramatic last-ball boundary to win a thrilling One-Day Cup final and shatter Hampshire's hopes of silverware.
body: The Blaze, who had already won the T20 Blast and County Cup trophies this season, seemed to be coasting towards their target of 252 after half-centuries from Tammy Beaumont (74) and Georgia Elwiss (64) at the Utilita Bowl.
But Hampshire's spinners fought back, with Amanda-Jade Wellington taking 3-36 and Bex Tyson 2-46 as four wickets went down for 29 to leave the Blaze needing 30 from the final three overs.
However, Jones kept her cool with an unbeaten 34 from 25 balls and, with two still required from Daisy Gibb's final delivery, pulled it to the boundary to clinch a remarkable treble for her side.
That meant heartbreak for Hampshire on home soil for a second successive year, having lost the 2025 final to Lancashire.

articles.title: Whether by accident or design, Thierno Barry is the face of the new Everton
articles.summary: Everton 1-0 Ipswich: While others in the Premier League confused themselves with spending sprees, David Moyes’ side are making the most of what they have
body: Everton have a gleaming £800m stadium but they can be the proof money isn't everything. In a division of conspicuous consumption, they were a club who struggled to spend. With their transfer-market profit, they finished low down the spending charts. But they are now fifth in the actual table, three points off the top, after an unbeaten start.

If the question is whether that has come by accident or design, the same may be said of Thierno Barry 's winner against Ipswich. An impressive start may have come in spite of some of the powerbrokers at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but because of David Moyes. On days such as this, his virtues and values can feel timeless. His capacity to outperform relatively modest resources and galvanise relatively small squads has been proven time and again. If Everton were written off, they are scripting their own underdog story. "We have tried to turn it into a positive," said Moyes.

articles.title: Peterborough part ways with manager Luke Williams
articles.summary: Peterborough United have parted company with manager Luke Williams following Saturday’s disappointing 2-0 home defeat by Doncaster Rovers, a result which left Posh second from bottom of League One. Williams had been in charge for 11 months, overseeing 47 competitive matches.
body: The defeat to Doncaster, who began the day at the foot of the table, was Peterborough’s third in a five-game winless league run. They are now just one point above bottom club Wigan Athletic.

Williams, 45, initially made a positive impression after replacing Darren Ferguson but struggled to find consistency with a young squad. His recent comments in interviews had also frustrated supporters, with boos greeting the team at half-time and full-time on Saturday.
There was one notable success during his tenure, as Peterborough reached the Carabao Cup fourth round after beating Barnsley on penalties.

articles.title: England swat aside Sri Lanka to return to top of T20 world rankings
articles.summary: England returned to the top of the T20 world rankings as they earned arguably their most emphatic win yet in a series of drubbings dished out to Sri Lanka, beating the tourists by eight wickets at Emirates Old Trafford.
body: Off the back of 119-run and six-wicket wins in the opening two games, Harry Brook's side clinched a 3-0 series sweep as his 33 off 21 balls, plus Jos Buttler's unbeaten 62 off 32 fired the hosts to their 125-run target in a mere 9.4 overs.

Aneurin Donald (13 off 6) could only manage a brief cameo with the bat for the third time in the series - stumped off Tharindu Ratnayake - while Brook was run out just shy of victory, one that Buttler clinched with a stunning one-handed six over deep midwicket to make it 15 wins in a row for England against Sri Lanka in T20 internationals.

articles.title: McIlroy two off pace as Elvira and Celli share Wentworth lead
articles.summary: Manuel Elvira and Filippo Celli share the lead heading into the final round of the BMW PGA Championship after they both made birdies on the 18th to move one ahead at Wentworth.
body: Rather remarkably, 20 players will go into Sunday within four shots of the lead, including Rory McIlroy, who produced a box-office finish, sending the patrons into delirium on the 18th by making an eagle to move within two shots of the pace-setting duo at 11 under par.
McIlroy equalled four other players - Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan - to finish tied for sixth on the leaderboard through 54 holes.
In windy conditions, Spain's Alejandro Del Rey and American duo Johannes Veerman and JJ Spaun had all been tied with Celli and Elvira at 12 under par late in the third round.
Del Rey and Veerman had enjoyed epic days on the course, each shooting low scores of eight-under 64 to shoot up the leaderboard.
